about.title: About

research.title: Virtual Context Stacking

cameras.text: Multi-camera tracking usually runs every camera on its own, then needs geometric calibration and a re-identification network to decide which car is which across views.
cameras.caption: Three camera views, as the thesis tool loads them.

frame.text: I normalised the regions that matter from every camera into one composite frame. One pass now covers every view: one pipeline instead of N.
frame.caption: The same views, stacked into one composite frame.

tracked.text: A detector and ByteTrack run once on the composite, with no re-identification network. In the thesis, with YOLO11, that held 81.3% cross-view identity consistency at 30 FPS.
tracked.caption: Detections on the composite frame, as the tool shows them.

hsgf.title: Hybrid Semantic-Governance Framework (HSGF)
points: Trackers swap identities under occlusion. HSGF uses language attributes ("silver sedan") from a local vision-language model, Florence-2, to audit and veto wrong track merges.
Pipeline: YOLO11 and OC-SORT for tracking, Florence-2 for attributes, LanceDB as the vector store.
Working proof-of-concept that detects identity conflicts in offline tests.

thesis.title: Virtual Context Stacking
thesis.org: MSc thesis on multi-camera vehicle tracking, Sakarya University
points: Multi-camera tracking usually needs geometric calibration and a heavy re-identification network. I normalised regions from every camera into one composite frame, so a single pass tracks across all views: one pipeline instead of N.
YOLO11 and ByteTrack, with no explicit re-identification network.
81.3% cross-view identity consistency at 30 FPS on standard hardware.
Published at the 3rd International Ankara Scientific Research and Innovation Congress (July 2025). Advisor: Prof. Dr. Ahmet Özmen.
